thread.title: TSA now allows some gateside greetings with PreCheck - NewsBreak
thread.title_full: TSA now allows some gateside greetings with PreCheck - NewsBreak

author: Erin Alberty
title: TSA now allows some gateside greetings with PreCheck - NewsBreak
text:
By Erin Alberty ,
8 hours ago
The Salt Lake airport is now allowing gateside goodbyes and reunions under a new TSA plan to let PreCheck members through airport security even if they aren't flying.
Why it matters: The program allows more airport access than traditional gate passes, which are only available in a few circumstances like meeting an unaccompanied child or helping travelers with disabilities.
Gateside passes allow non-travelers to use PreCheck lanes to meet a friend or conduct business during a layover; shop or eat beyond security; or welcome loved ones as they deplane. Catch up quick: PreCheck is one of TSA's fast-track security options that funnels passengers into their own lines with fewer screening steps if they are approved after undergoing a background check.
Driving the news: Applications opened this week for "Gateside by TSA PreCheck" access at 13 airports, including SLC.
How it works: Click "apply" here 1-3 days before you want to go to the airport, and create or open your login.gov account. If you're bringing children, include that on your application.
Approval will appear on your account dashboard. Bring your usual ID to the TSA PreCheck lanes at the airport. If children are with you, you'll need to log into your dashboard to show the approval. The intrigue: SLC arrivals are known for enthusiastic homecomings — especially for returning missionaries with the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints.
The new airport added a gathering room near baggage claim for crowds that sometimes greet missionaries with signs, balloons, hugs and even choreographed dances . Those events could spread deeper into the terminal — but only if everyone in the group has PreCheck status and applied for Gateside access in advance. What we're watching: Whether SLC's mercifully short PreCheck lines get longer now that more people have a reason to use them.
